messages.subject: Converting absolute to relative measurements
parts:
This is more of a data manipulation question than a plotting question.
I have a bunch of data in discrete bins. The bins are ordered:
treatment K includes the effects of treatments 1 through K-1 as well.
There is also a sub-bin classification which is not ordered. I want
to transform the data to be relative to the median of bin 0.
Currently I'm doing it like this:

d <- read.table('data.tab', header=TRUE)
d$patch <- ordered(d$patch, levels=unique(levels(d$patch)[d$patch]))

ms <- cast(subset(d, patch==levels(patch)[1]),
value='time', entry ~ ., fun.aggregate='median')
mv <- ms$`(all)`
names(mv) <- ms$entry
rm(ms)

d <- ddply(d, .(patch, entry), function(x) transform(x, reltime = time
- mv[entry]))

'patch' is the id variable for the ordered bins, and 'entry' is the id
variable for the unordered sub-bin classification, just to be clear.
It seems like there ought to be a more elegant way to do some of these
operations, particularly forcing ordering for the 'patch' column in
the initial data set, and constructing the 'mv' vector. Any
suggestions?

Thanks,
zw

messages.subject: Re: Converting absolute to relative measurements
parts:
Hi Zack.

How about

ddply(d, c("patch", "entry"), transform,
reltime = time - median(time[patch == 0]))

?

Hadley

messages.subject: Re: Converting absolute to relative measurements
parts:
Doesn't work; I get NAs for all but the first bin, because inside
ddply, only one level of 'patch' is visible, so
time[patch==levels(patch)[1]] is an empty vector for most bins.

(time[patch==0] is always an empty vector with my version of R.)

zw
